media.notes: Figure 16. Preserved paratype female Tropijotus galacticus sp. nov. (QM). A dorsal view B ventral view (scale bars: 1mm). C dissected epigyne, ventral view E dissected epigyne, dorsal view. Abbreviations: AS = anterior spermatheca, CD = copulatory duct, CO = copulatory opening, F = fossa, FD = fertilisation duct, MS = median septum, PS = posterior spermatheca. Epigynum. Epigynum with a pair of large, ovate fossae separated by a narrow septum. Posterior spermathecae medium-sized, sub-ovate, positioned at the posteromedial margin of each fossa. Copulatory ducts narrow and elongate, arising from the anteromedial margin of each posterior spermatheca, extending anteriorly before making a sharp turn at the internal anterolateral margin of each fossa, then continuing toward the anterior spermathecae. Anterior spermathecae round, smaller than the posterior spermathecae, situated just below the duct turn at the internal mediolateral margin of each fossa. Fertilization ducts slender, gently curved medially, with a slightly expanded, tapering distal portion, giving them a feather- or sickle-like appearance in dorsal view (Fig. 16C, D).

The molecular data specifically support the inclusion of Jotus chlorophthalmus comb. nov. and Jotus michaelseni comb. nov. within the genus. In the case of Jotus vittatus comb. nov., its taxonomic placement was resolved through morphological analysis following our rediscovery of the syntype series in the Museums Victoria collection. The subsequent designation of a lectotype from this material stabilises the name and confirms its placement in Jotus.
